test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 23 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following features is correct regarding the federal system of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Equal representation of all states in the upper house of parliament
Equal representation of all states in the lower house of parliament

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dual government**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution establishes a **dual government** system, also known as **federalism**, where **powers are divided between the central government and the state governments**.
 
• Unlike some other federal systems, India does not have **dual citizenship**; citizens are only recognized as Indian citizens.
 
• **Representation in the upper house of parliament** (Rajya Sabha) is **based on the population of each state**, not equal representation.
 
• **Representation in the lower house of parliament** (Lok Sabha) is also **based on population**, ensuring more populous states have more representatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains **three lists** which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• **Amendments to the Constitution** can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
